LESSON: NUMBER SEQUENCING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: NUMBERS
Topic 2.4: Number sequencing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Number sequencing, part of NUMBERS in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How do you identify number symbols? 2. How do you arrange number cards in sequence 3. Why do you arrange numbers in sequence?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Number sequencing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination: communication and self-expression: The learner communicates ideas with confidence while working

in pairs or in groups as they arrange numbers in sequence and using the sequencing skills to complete number puzzles.

Values:
• Peace: The learner harmoniously sings songs on number sequence comprising numbers 1-9.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Hygiene: The learner observes hygiene while sequencing number cards by not putting the cards in the mouth because they are

dirty.

Link to other activity areas:

• Creative Activities: The concept of pattern is reinforced as the learner completes a number puzzle related to number sequencing.

Suggested Resources:

Number cards, number chart, number cut out, braille number cards.
